skill.name: finishing-a-development-branch
skill.description: Guides agents through final branch checks, merge or PR choices, and cleanup decisions after implementation work is complete.
skill.summary: Guides tested branch completion with merge, PR, keep, or discard options.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The scanner flagged many markdown fences as Ruby backtick execution, and most of those are false positives. Real risk remains in state-changing git commands, remote PR creation, destructive cleanup, and conflicting worktree guidance. No evidence of prompt injection or secret exfiltration was found.

remediation.issue: Option 2 cleanup guidance conflicts across the skill.
remediation.suggestion: Make the PR workflow consistent about whether the worktree is preserved or removed, then update Step 5 and the quick reference.

remediation.issue: Discard and cleanup steps can delete branches or worktrees.
remediation.suggestion: Keep typed confirmation and require a final display of the exact branch, commit list, and worktree path before deletion.

remediation.issue: Shell examples use placeholder branch, title, and path values.
remediation.suggestion: Tell agents to validate and quote substituted values, or use structured command arguments when available.

remediation.issue: The PR example uses shell command substitution for body text.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer a reviewed body file or an explicit body argument to reduce shell expansion mistakes.

semantic_findings.title: Conflicting Worktree Cleanup Instructions
semantic_findings.description: The PR path says to clean up the worktree, while later guidance says PR worktrees should be kept. This contradiction can cause unexpected worktree removal after a pull request.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The contradictory instructions are explicit in the cited lines. The impact is likely data loss or workflow disruption, not secret exposure.

semantic_findings.title: Destructive Branch and Worktree Cleanup
semantic_findings.description: The skill includes force branch deletion and worktree removal steps. The discard flow requests typed confirmation, but the commands can permanently remove local development work.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file directly instructs branch deletion and worktree removal. Confirmation steps reduce likelihood but do not remove destructive impact.

content.value_statement: Finished branches still need tests, merge decisions, and cleanup. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through a structured completion workflow.
actual_capabilities: Prompts the agent to run the project test suite before merge or PR steps.
Helps identify a likely base branch from main or master.
Presents four completion choices: local merge, pull request, keep branch, or discard work.
Provides command examples for merge, push, pull request creation, and cleanup.
Requires typed confirmation before discarding branch work.
limitations: Assumes git is available and the repository is in a valid branch state.
Uses generic test command examples that must be adapted to each project.
Does not resolve merge conflicts or failed tests automatically.
Includes destructive cleanup commands that require careful user review.

use_cases.title: Complete Feature Work
use_cases.description: Verify tests, choose a completion path, and avoid leaving stale development branches behind.

use_cases.title: Open a Pull Request
use_cases.description: Prepare a finished branch for review with a concise summary and test plan.

use_cases.title: Clean Up Worktrees
use_cases.description: Remove finished branch worktrees only after the user selects a cleanup path.

prompt_templates.title: Finish My Branch
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the finishing-a-development-branch skill. Verify tests, then show me the completion options for this branch.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Pull Request
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill after tests pass. Prepare the branch for a pull request and include a concise PR summary and test plan.

prompt_templates.title: Merge Locally With Cleanup
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to verify tests, identify the base branch, merge locally, rerun tests, and clean up the finished branch.

prompt_templates.title: Review Every Final Step
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill and explain each repository operation before execution. Stop before destructive cleanup unless I type the exact confirmation.

output_examples.input: Implementation is finished and tests appear ready.
output: Tests passed and the branch appears to split from main.
Options presented: merge locally, create PR, keep branch, or discard work.
Waiting for user choice before changing repository state.

output_examples.input: The user selected the pull request path.
output: Branch pushed to the remote repository.
Pull request prepared with summary and test plan.
Worktree handling follows the selected cleanup policy.

output_examples.input: The user selected discard and confirmed the exact word.
output: Branch and worktree targets displayed before removal.
Discard action completed only after typed confirmation.
Final status reported with remaining branch information.

best_practices: Run tests before selecting any completion path.
Review branch names, base branch, and worktree path before executing cleanup.
Use typed confirmation for every discard operation.
anti_patterns: Do not merge or open a PR while tests are failing.
Do not delete branches or worktrees without showing what will be removed.
Do not treat the command examples as a replacement for project-specific checks.

faq.question: Does this skill run tests automatically?
faq.answer: It prompts the agent to run the project test suite before offering merge or PR options.

faq.question: Can it create a pull request?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a workflow for pushing the branch and preparing a PR summary and test plan.

faq.question: Can it discard local work?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires exact typed confirmation before discard steps should run.

faq.question: Does it resolve merge conflicts?
faq.answer: No. It can guide the workflow, but conflict resolution remains project-specific work.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is it safe for shared branches?
faq.answer: Use care. Review the base branch, remote target, and cleanup steps before changing shared branch state.
